Episode 232. Awakening (1)
Kwaaaaaa-!
Paelito let out a monstrous scream, pushing Jin back. Jin stumbled back, his arm almost twisted.
A chunk of fire, driven by the recoil, blocked Paelito's view momentarily. As he tried to clear the flames and charge forward, Bradamante dropped, splitting the fire in two.
Bradamante precisely aimed at Paelito's crown, but it lacked the strength to pierce Paelito's magical barrier, merely bouncing off and leaving a scratch on the shield.
‘I... didn't perceive it?’
For Paelito, it was nothing short of shocking.

It was an unexpected counterattack, yet neither quick nor sharp. Jin's sword had become dull, having lost an arm and severely injured. Even when compared to the ordinary strike of a novice who had just begun to understand the sword, it was no better.
But he didn't perceive the incoming sword.
Had there been no shield, had Jin possessed his usual strength, his whole body might have been cleaved in two. A chill ran down his spine.
‘Is it because of Simma? Even so, such an ordinary sword...!’
An incomprehensible event.
Anger at it was driving Paelito mad. Sakiel's death, Jin's ridiculous counterattack, and the fact that Jin was a regressor.
He couldn't accept it. Only by slaying Jin Lun Candel, that blazing monster, would this nightmare end.
The Hwangcheon Sword, Baskalara, became hazy.
But now, the forced sensory disruption had little effect on Jin. His vision had been half darkened for a while, and his shattered body was not precisely controlled.
Even with the characteristics of the Hwangcheon Sword, the feeling of dullness only grew. Whether he opened or closed his eyes, everything was dark, and wherever he looked, Paelito was there.
A swordmaster intoxicated with rage, hatred, and madness.
"Die, I said die!"
Screeech! The two swords intertwined, emitting a sharp metallic sound that pierced the eardrums. The two men leaned into each other as their sword clashes vibrated.
Winning such a power struggle was impossible for Jin. Paelito flung the sword to the side, leaving Jin defenseless and struck his face with his fist.

A dull and heavy sound, as if a rock had burst from within, echoed. The sensation of his forehead bone shattering vividly rang through Paelrito's fist, and Jin was knocked back a great distance, crashing into the ground.
"Cough!"
It felt as if something filled with blood had exploded inside his head. Blood splattered out of his eyes, ears, and mouth, momentarily blocking all sensations.
Paelrito, without hiding his urgency, lunged at Jin like a beast. If Jin was momentarily unconscious now, he wouldn't miss this chance.
"Die, Jin Lun Kendel, die!"
But as Paelrito closed the distance with Jin, he had to tightly close his eyes.

Again, out of nowhere, a flash bomb that Jin had formed in his palm was ablaze. The moment Paelrito's punch knocked him to the ground, Jin had dropped his sword and formed a flash bomb in his empty hand.
It was a behavior purely driven by instinct.
For Chansung, it was a shallow tactic that could never pass off as a coincidence. However, Paelrito felt a burning sensation in his eyes, exposed directly to the flash bomb.
Something invisible seemed to keep distorting the situation. Things that shouldn't have happened were repeating.
Jin barely regained consciousness while Paelrito hesitated. His vision, which had been dark, was now drenched in blood, presenting an entirely crimson landscape.
Breathing wasn't easy due to the clots of blood in his nose and throat. Still, he picked up his sword again, ignited the flames, and took his stance.
He vowed to transcend destiny.

He had decided to bear the burden of numerous historical changes and deaths caused by his return. He made up his mind to shoulder all the grief of the loved ones who fell in this battle, and the sorrow of those who would be left behind.
Therefore, even if his body shattered, he could not stop fighting.
Even if inevitable death approached, he had no choice but to fight. Just like Ron Hyran, whom he had admired in the past, Jin was now transcending death.
'His heart rate is getting faster.'

Paelrito, opening his eyes, took big strides towards Jin. With every step he took, he could hear his heartbeat as if his ear was pressed against his chest. He wanted to tear out the barely breathing heart and squeeze it with both hands.
He could have done it anytime. If only this incomprehensible phenomenon, as if he was carrying the blessing of the sun god, would stop.
'Wait, the blessing of the sun god... could it be the light that was revealed when he declared himself a returnee?'
A strange thought came to mind.
There's no way, the Sun God is already dead and Zito is set to become the new order of the world.
It seemed like the shadow of the cruel creator who drove the demons underground was enveloping Jin. The illusion was so vivid, it was chilling, and Paelrito wanted to step back.
He wanted to run away. A fear he had never felt since becoming a swordsman, no.
An inexplicable primal fear was freezing him. The grip of the sword in his hand was trembling, and his legs on the ground were wobbly.
"Sun God, you say...! Sun God, you say!? Stop with the nonsense, I am the sword. I am the only sword that has received the grace of pain!"
Like a child ignoring his fear, Paelrito forced himself to get past the light.
He moved forward, pushing through the frightening illusion. The one standing behind this illusion will soon become dust and disappear.
He wasn't wrong in his thinking.
A little later, Paelrito was able to face Jin, who was barely standing with his sword held tightly as if he were hugging it. His energy was sparse, left in patches like the fur of a sick animal.
"Ha, hahaha. Jin Lunkandel, can you say the same now? About surpassing fate, try babbling that again!"
The voice consumed by the devil and the original voice were mixed. His expression distorted, then calmed repeatedly, as if Jin was overcoming death, Paelrito was fighting the devil as well.
No response came from Jin.
Both the vocal cords and the lungs have almost lost their functions. Jin could not even perceive Paelrito approaching and wildly swung his sword into the air.
For a while, Paelrito watched him and burst into laughter. He leaned on his knees, holding his forehead, spitting out wind-blown laughter.
"Yes, that's how you, a human, should look. You said you died and went back in time? That the regression is superior to all fate? Never, you were just drunk on luck you shouldn't have gotten."
Paelrito fired his sword aura. It wasn't the sword of annihilation, but the sword aura that he had been spreading non-stop throughout the battle.
Even that was too much for Jin now. The body that was touched by the sword aura fell to the ground as if a dry pile of dirt had collapsed.
The first thing to fall were two fingers holding the sword. No flesh, blood, or bone was visible. The cross section of the amputated part was just an empty darkness.

The remaining three fingers also seemed to lose their strength, and the shaking Bradamante continued in an unstable manner. If you go and push it slightly, all the fingers will disintegrate and the sword will fall to the ground.
It was then that Paelrito could finally calm down.
He escaped from the fear of unknown origin and was able to face reality. All he saw were the end words of a stubborn human being, no different from a carcass.
Upon facing Jin, Paelleto felt a sense of solitude, as if he had been abandoned on an island, as if he had been the only survivor facing imminent extinction.

He was engulfed in such solitude. Nowhere in those feelings was there any joy of ultimate victory. As Jin had said, all that awaited the victor was an unforgettably painful scar, even after death, which was rather eerie.
"......You can't transcend anything. There will never be anyone like you in this world again. No one can carry on your will, and no one can escape from their predetermined life."
The Bascara turned black.
But it wasn't easy to stab Jin. Paelleto hesitated for a while, just staring at Jin.

It wasn't because of the fear created by the illusion of the Sun God. It wasn't because he was so exhausted he couldn't even swing his sword. Paelleto still had the confidence that he could kill all the bugs left in the kingdom by himself.
What stopped Paelleto now was the thought that death could actually make things easier for him.

He didn't think Jin's soul would go to hell. Even if he were to swallow him with Bascara, he didn't think the beings sealed inside, like Visa, could defeat Jin. Rather, Jin might resurrect from within and break through Bascara.
Because the order of suffering has not yet been established in the world. Until that order is fully in place, he felt that Jin could not be sealed in any way.
It wasn't a feeling, but a conviction.
However, Paelleto decided not to annihilate Jin. Even if there was a future mishap where Jin broke the seal of Bascara, he had to hold onto his soul for now.

So he had to show him. He had to show him a world where order has been established, bugs struggling under the ceiling of fate, how the world he loved, everything he took responsibility for, had finally met their end.
"Shout out when you wake up again."
Thud...!
Bascara pierced Jin's chest. Black blood flowed from his heart, which had already cooled and stopped.
All that was left was for Bascara to open and swallow Jin. Bascara will seal Jin's will, his soul, that was overcoming death, and postpone his annihilation.
The sealing ends in a few seconds.
However, the magical tendrils spreading from Bascara's blade were blocked by something, unable to bind Jin.
A moment later, Paelleto was able to realize why.
There was a person bowing her head, resting her forehead on Jin's back.
"Jin, I'm here. I, the kingdom, the people are here."
Queen Rani.
She was praying behind Jin.
